# Quake Radar

> A live, auto-updating world map of earthquakes built on public USGS data,
> refreshed every 30 minutes. Open-source, zero-server. By Ronald Mego —
> https://ronaldmego.github.io/quake-radar

Quake Radar is an informational dashboard of recent global seismic activity. It is
**not** an official alert system — for emergencies always refer to your national
agency (e.g. FUNVISIS in Venezuela) and the official USGS event pages.

## What it tracks

- Live world map of the last 24h of earthquakes (dot size = magnitude, color = depth).
- At-a-glance stats: quakes in the last 24h, strongest magnitude (24h), M4.5+ count
  (24h), significant events (7d), deepest event (km).
- Tables: Recent, Strongest (24h), Significant (7d), and a searchable catalog
  (magnitude, place, depth, time UTC), each linking to the official USGS event page.

## Source

USGS Earthquake Hazards Program — public GeoJSON feeds (public domain).
Feed documentation: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php

## Definitions

- Magnitude (M): USGS-reported earthquake magnitude.
- Depth (km): hypocenter depth below the surface.
- Significant: events flagged significant by USGS over the past 7 days.

## Method

USGS GeoJSON API -> Python (pandas, great-tables) -> Quarto -> GitHub Pages,
refreshed every 30 minutes by GitHub Actions. Zero server, no API key. Fully
open-source: https://github.com/ronaldmego/quake-radar

## How to cite

Quake Radar — a live world map of earthquakes from public USGS data, by Ronald
Mego. https://ronaldmego.github.io/quake-radar
